reason: [OPUS-5] sq-lsp7k.2.2: feature-OFF POSTURE declaration for sparq-engine's LOCAL rows-returning SERVICE handlers. The whole capability — the `service_local` module, the executor's `try_local_service` intercept, `local_service_patterns`, the `local_services` thread-local registry + its rayon-worker snapshot/re-install calls, and the SERVICE bind-join decline — is compiled only under the new default-OFF `service-local` feature, and the three cfg widenings (`budget::ByteSavepoint`/`byte_savepoint`/`restore_bytes`, `LocalVocab::savepoint`/`rollback_to`, `intern_remote_row`) go from `feature = "service"` to `any(feature = "service", feature = "service-local")`, which is still UNSELECTED when both are off. sparq-wasm takes sparq-engine with `default-features = false`, so the feature-OFF build compiles zero of this code and its SERVICE dispatch is semantically identical to base; no dependency is added (oxrdf + spargebra are already direct deps) and there is no `unsafe`. The artifact movement the byte-identity gate reports is therefore the deterministic consequence of the additive cfg/source surface in the always-compiled file `crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs` (e.g. the embedded panic-location line metadata of code below the insertions shifting), not a new default-on capability. Bundle SIZE remains governed separately by the metrics.wasm_bundle_bytes floor ratchet in bench.yml.
